address: Ashley Heights, 4 Ashley Close, Sevenoaks, Kent
postcode_basis: TN13 3AP is recorded in the retained agent listing (source/agent-listing.html). Confirm the site address against the title register; the recorded applicant name/address remain working assumptions.
application_type: Householder planning application (Town and Country Planning Act 1990)
proposal_description: Erection of a two-storey extension with rooms in the roof and a basement beneath, forming a new principal elevation to Ashley Close, together with a first-floor and roof extension to the side wing, a rear dormer, a single-storey rear garden room with terrace over, open-sided garden loggia adjoining the retained outbuildings, new swimming pool and sunken spa, detached garden workshop, and alterations to fenestration, forecourt, boundary wall and gate, following removal of the porch, chimney and front boundary piers. The side-extension front wall and roof edge are set back 450 mm from the original front alignment, keeping the retained house frontage visually prominent.
north_basis: Least-squares registration of the model to the north-up OS extract (proposal/street-registration/registration.json): model +x bears 82.65°, so model +y bears 352.9°. Confirm against the purchased OS extract.
red_line_source: navigation.site.outline_m (HM Land Registry title plan K568939 traced and registered)
rear_strip_basis: The rear garden strip is drawn inside the same red line as on the title plan; the coloured strips at its north-west corner on the title plan are rights of way, not separate titles — verify against the register.

designations.basis: Green Belt: owner confirms the site is outside. Read-only Sevenoaks public GIS screening on 25 September 2026, using the existing approximate model-to-BNG registration, shows no plot overlap with The Vine conservation area or nearby Article 4 areas. These are map checks, not formal land-charge verification. TPO 19/1987 (T4 cherry and G1 group) is mapped beside the east/rear boundary; legal coverage, surviving tree identity and root protection require survey and council/arboricultural confirmation. Historic England NHLE screening finds no listed-building point/polygon on the reconstructed plot; this does not determine curtilage, setting or local listing. Current Environment Agency flood-zone data returns no Zone 2/3 polygon within the plot plus 100 m, supporting river/sea Flood Zone 1 map screening. Natural England boundary screening places the plot outside Kent Downs National Landscape, about 675 m away; setting effects are not assessed. Environment Agency surface-water spatial-planning WMS screening shows no mapped extent across the approximate plot in the present-day or 2070s upper-end climate scenarios; these are area-level datasets, not an individual-property flood assessment. Local-list status, groundwater, sewer flooding, drainage changes and basement suitability remain unverified. See proposal/redesigns/research/RESEARCH.md.

original_dwelling.basis: The existing house is treated as the original dwelling as first built (post-1948, unextended); no previous extensions are known.

existing_drawings_basis: Existing drawings are a model reconstruction from the estate-agent floor plan, aerial and photographic sources, validated against the 34 published room dimensions; heights are photo-fitted (floor-to-floor 2.80 m, eaves 5.35 m, ridge 8.05 m). To be confirmed by measured survey before submission.
levels_basis: Site terrain and ground levels are model estimates, not a measured topographical survey; verify all levels, thresholds and boundaries.

bins_cycles.location: Within the double garage (two bins, two cycles); collection point at the gate

renewables.note: None proposed at planning stage; any air-source heat pump or PV to be added under permitted development or a later application.

parking.existing_spaces_note: 4 forecourt spaces; garage capacity to verify
parking.basis: Three forecourt bays and two garage spaces in the proposal. The existing forecourt holds four cars informally; existing garage capacity requires verification.

visibility_splays.basis: The shown 2.4 m x 25 m splay is an unverified concept, not an accepted 30 mph design. Manual for Streets Table 7.1 gives 25 m at 20 mph and 43 m at 30 mph. Confirm observed speeds, highway geometry and the required splays with KCC Highways.

trees.basis: Tree positions are the modelled trunks (photographic reconstruction); species and dimensions are estimates for this issue. A BS5837 survey is required.

materials.roof: Natural slate, anthracite (existing slate retained where shown)
materials.dormers: Tile-hung cheeks and front panels matching the roof tiles; dark flat roof membrane and metal flashings; black window frames. Dormers remain tiled in both viewer wall-finish choices.
materials.windows_doors: Bronze-black powder-coated aluminium frames, clear double glazing; pale oak external doors
materials.hard_landscape: Resin-bound gravel forecourt, limestone paving, permeable court paving
materials.boundary: Red-brown brick front wall 1.95 m (26 courses), with oak-slatted sliding gate; existing fences and hedges retained
materials.privacy: Roof terrace west edge: 1.8 m opal laminated glass screen in bronze-black posts (replaces the timber guard on that edge). Side-wing west bedroom windows and new-wing east windows facing neighbours obscure-glazed below 1.7 m.

front_wing_case.summary: The new wing is two storeys with rooms in the roof: its eaves (5.35 m) and ridge (8.05 m) are the same as the existing two-storey house, and the loft rooms sit within that roof behind a flat-topped dormer. The plot sits at the head of the Ashley Close cul-de-sac, so the wing is designed as the house's new principal elevation towards the turning head rather than as a front extension of the retained house: its south gable stands parallel to the front boundary wall and faces the turning head, the entrance moves into it, and the retained house reads as the rear range behind the courtyard.
front_wing_case.basis: Owner's position (22 September): the front elevation of the house is being re-formed; because the plot closes the cul-de-sac the wing faces the road as a new frontage rather than projecting in front of a building line shared with neighbours.

precedents.address: Meadowfield, 60 Hitchen Hatch Lane, Sevenoaks TN13 3AU
precedents.decision: Granted by Development Control Committee (2021; referred by a councillor on neighbour amenity, officers recommended approval)
precedents.description: Demolition of garage and shed; remodelling and enhancement including extensions to the existing house, new porch, integral garage, loft conversion, landscaping, covered pergola, rooflights and alterations to fenestration
precedents.relevance: A whole-house remodel keeping the existing house, on the road bounding Ashley Close. The committee report found that the extension, 'whilst not set down from the ridge height of the main house, would incorporate the existing roof form, therefore considered to reflect the character of the existing dwelling', and that it would not 'significantly alter the existing residential and built up character of the area'. Mature landscaping screening it from the street weighed in its favour. Assessed under Core Strategy SP1, ADMP EN1/EN2/T2 and the Residential Extensions SPD.
precedents.policies: Core Strategy SP1, ADMP EN1, EN2, T2, Residential Extensions SPD

precedents.description: Two storey front extension with front porch; alteration to fenestration
precedents.relevance: Adjoining road (Hitchen Hatch Lane bounds Ashley Close to the north); same Urban Confines and Sevenoaks Residential Character Area constraints. The officer's test was whether the front extension would 'significantly lessen the set-back nature' of the properties lining that section of the road, and whether it was subservient in scale with a common gabled design. Obscure glazing in the flank was accepted as the privacy answer.
